title: Beef Rendang
subtitle: Slow-cooked beef in rich coconut and spice paste
excerpt: Beef chuck is simmered for two hours in a coconut milk broth loaded with aromatics until the liquid evaporates and the meat fries gently in the remaining fat. The result is intensely flavoured, tender beef. This dish is worth the time.
sourceNotes: Based on the dry rendang style of West Sumatra and Malaysia. Lemongrass is traditional but not widely stocked; lemon zest is used here to provide a similar citrus note.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions. Reheat slowly on the hob with a splash of water.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Rendang improves significantly the next day as the spices deepen.

content.text: Traditional rendang uses lemongrass. This recipe uses the zest of one lemon to bring a similar citrus note. The result is very close. Don't rush the final frying stage where the beef browns in the coconut fat.

items.prepNote: zest only, as a substitute for lemongrass

content.text: Put the onion, garlic, ginger, lemon zest, chilli flakes, gochugaru, cumin, and coriander in a blender. Add 3 tbsp water and blend to a smooth paste.
Heat the oil in a large stockpot over medium heat. Fry the paste for 5 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant and slightly darkened.
Add the beef. Stir to coat in the paste.
Pour in the coconut milk. Add the star anise, cloves, cinnamon, kaffir lime leaves, and palm sugar. Stir everything together.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer. Cook uncovered for 60 minutes, stirring every 15 minutes.
Continue simmering for another 30 to 40 minutes. The liquid will reduce dramatically. Keep stirring so the bottom doesn't catch.
When almost all the liquid is gone, the beef will start frying in the coconut fat. Stir constantly for 10 to 15 minutes until the beef is dark and caramelised.
Remove the star anise, cloves, and lime leaves. Taste and adjust salt. Serve with steamed rice.

items.cause: Simmer was too vigorous and dried out the meat
items.fix: Add 100ml water, cover, and cook 20 more minutes.

items.symptom: Sauce has caught on the bottom
items.cause: Not stirred enough during the dry-fry stage
items.fix: Deglaze with 2 tbsp water and scrape the bottom.

items.cause: Palm sugar not added, or too little salt
items.fix: Add a pinch of salt and a little more palm sugar.
